text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The newspaper editorial says the situation in the country is resembling that just before last year's polls because of President Sali Berisha's alleged attempt to postpone the elections in a bid to increase his share of the vote.
- The newspaper publisher says the republican guard under Berisha's control surrounded his home and threatened him.
- Political parties cannot finalise their list of candidates because a committee set up to verify their background has not yet replied to them, thereby endangering planned elections on June 29.
- New multinational troops to arrive in Albania on June 20.
- The centre-right Democratic Alliance party called for a "Contract for Albania", including a broad-based post-election government that excludes Berisha's Democratic party.
- The National Front and the Republican parties turned down Berisha's request to form an alliance with his Democrats.
- Brian Pridham, a senior OSCE official in Albania, resigned for personal reasons.
- 600 international observers will cover some 80 percent of the ballot boxes in the elections. The multinational force will stay in Albania for 45 more days.
- Foreign ministers of seven Balkan countries meeting in Greece called on Albania to take the country back to a normal situation.
- Jeff Briggs, the British diplomat stabbed on Monday, said the incident had private motives and declined any further comment on it to the Italian police.
- A poll conducted in Tirana by the Eureka foundation showed 24.2 percent of voters would support monarchy in the June 29 referendum.
- The newspaper editorial attacks the Socialist leader Fatos Nano for using a "super-lie" about the return of the money lost in the pyramid schemes just to gain power.
- Smaller parties, complaining about the distribution of proportional seats, ask Berisha to convene a ten-party roundtable to discuss the issue.
- Prime Minister Baskim Fino says in an interview with the newspaper the elections were the only solution for the country's future.
